1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/runtime-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 Runtime prefetching extends the static shell with request-specific content like the user's name from a cookie, by invoking the route at prefetch time. Ensuring navigations are instant is the foundation: a route that doesn't navigate instantly without runtime prefetching won't navigate instantly with it either. See [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## The tools 42 43 ### Build the static shell 44 45 With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell. 46 47 > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the runtime prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 48 49 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 50 51 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. With [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), the information is available and such a fallback becomes part of the instant UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 52 53 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route: a fallback that renders instantly during client navigations when nothing else is ready. See [App Shells](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#app-shells) for how to enable them and how they pair with runtime prefetching. 54 55 ### Tune what `` prefetches 56 57 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. The shell is shared across every link to the same route, so rendering a `` is effectively free. 58 59 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 60 61 ```tsx 62 63 Checkout 64 65 ``` 66 67 To prefetch with the user's session (cookies, headers, the full URL), opt the destination segment into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) with `export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'`. 68 69 ### Validate instant navigation 70 71 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 72 73 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 74 75 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 76 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 77 78 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 79 cacheComponents: true, 80 experimental: { 81 instantInsights: { 82 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 83 }, 84 }, 85 } 86 87 export default nextConfig 88 ``` 89 90
91 How validation simulates different navigations 92 93 For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 94 95 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 96 97 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 98 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 99 100 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 101 102
103 104 ### Test it in CI 105 106 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern. 107 108 ### Inspect loading states 109 110 The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell. 111 112 Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow. 113 114 See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell. 115 116 ## A page that navigates instantly 117 118 To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant. 119 120 The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory. 121 122 - There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time 123 - Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Hooks like `useSearchParams()` still need a `` boundary. 203 204 ## Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools 205 206 As you develop a route, the Next.js DevTools let you see what your users see on page loads and client navigations before dynamic data streams in. Use it to verify that your loading states look right, confirm the content you expect appears immediately, and iterate on where to place `` boundaries. 207 208 The [React DevTools Suspense panel](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) complements this: it lists the `` boundaries in the tree and lets you toggle each one between its fallback and resolved state, so you can see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. 209 210 {/* TODO: screenshot — React DevTools Suspense panel listing boundaries with toggle controls */} 211 212 The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 213 214 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4} 215 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 216 217 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 218 cacheComponents: true, 219 } 220 221 export default nextConfig 222 ``` 223 224 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then toggle **Pause on navigations**. The panel shows **Awaiting navigation...** With the toggle on, the next refresh or link click freezes the page so you can inspect the shell. 225 226 Refresh the product page. The Inspector freezes and shows **Loading shell** labeled **Page load** with the target URL. In the app, two fallbacks appear: "Loading product..." and "Checking availability...". Each navigation pauses as long as the toggle is on. 273 274 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params). 275 276 ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests 277 278 Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 279 280 The `@next/playwright` package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`: 281 282 ```bash package="pnpm" 283 pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 284 ``` 285 286 ```bash package="npm" 287 npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 288 ``` 289 290 ```bash package="yarn" 291 yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 292 ``` 293 294 ```bash package="bun" 295 bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 296 ``` 297 298 Then use it in a test: 299 300 ```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" 301 import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test' 302 import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 303 304 test('product title appears instantly', async ({ page }) => { 305 await page.goto('/store/shoes') 306 307 await instant(page, async () => { 308 await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]') 309 await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') 310 }) 311 312 // After instant() exits, dynamic content streams in 313 await expect(page.locator('text=in stock')).toBeVisible() 314 }) 315 ``` 316 317 Inside the `instant()` callback, only the static shell is visible. The featured section appears immediately, and **"Loading product..."** shows where the product details will stream in. 444 445 ### Iterate on loading states 446 447 {/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */} 448 449 Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation. 450 451 The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time. 452 453 Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent. 454 455 ## AI workflow 456 457 The observe-fix-iterate loop is well suited to AI coding agents: 458 459 - **Observe**: read validation insights in the dev overlay and dev server console. 460 - **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or ``). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation, whether that's in dev or a build. 461 - **Iterate**: run an `instant()` test to check what appears in the shell. Because the output is deterministic, the agent can assert on it without flaky retries. 462 463 The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model. It follows the insights and errors until they're gone. 464 465 For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down. You can hint at what data needs to be fresh on load and what can be cached, and the agent will move the `` and `use cache` placement accordingly. 466 467 Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers: 468 469 - **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell. 470 - **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile. 471 - **Runtime prefetching** (nav-only): when I/O depends on `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, opt the route into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) so the framework prerenders it at link-prefetch time. 472 473 Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. 1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/runtime-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 Runtime prefetching extends the static shell with request-specific content like the user's name from a cookie, by invoking the route at prefetch time. Ensuring navigations are instant is the foundation: a route that doesn't navigate instantly without runtime prefetching won't navigate instantly with it either. See [Runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## The tools 42 43 ### Build the static shell 44 45 With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell. 46 47 > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the runtime prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 48 49 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 50 51 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. With [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching), the information is available and such a fallback becomes part of the instant UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 52 53 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route: a fallback that renders instantly during client navigations when nothing else is ready. See [App Shells](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching#app-shells) for how to enable them and how they pair with runtime prefetching. 54 55 ### Tune what `` prefetches 56 57 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. The shell is shared across every link to the same route, so rendering a `` is effectively free. 58 59 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 60 61 ```tsx 62 63 Checkout 64 65 ``` 66 67 To prefetch with the user's session (cookies, headers, the full URL), opt the destination segment into [runtime prefetching](/docs/app/guides/runtime-prefetching) with `export const prefetch = 'allow-runtime'`. 68 69 ### Validate instant navigation 70 71 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 72 73 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 74 75 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 76 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 77 78 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 79 cacheComponents: true, 80 experimental: { 81 instantInsights: { 82 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 83 }, 84 }, 85 } 86 87 export default nextConfig 88 ``` 89 90
91 How validation simulates different navigations 92 93 For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 94 95 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 96 97 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 98 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 99 100 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 101 102
103 104 ### Test it in CI 105 106 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern. 107 108 ### Inspect loading states 109 110 The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell. 111 112 Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow. 113 114 See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell. 115 116 ## A page that navigates instantly 117 118 To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The db query is inside a `` boundary 126 127 ```tsx filename="app/store/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={7-12,31} 128 import { Suspense } from 'react' 129 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 130 131 export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>) { 132 return ( 133

On the first visit the cache is cold and both are visible. 227 228

The Inspector shows **Loading shell** labeled **Client nav** with both source and target URLs. In the app, the product name and price appear immediately (cached). They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 279 280 The `@next/playwright` package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Fixed — the product title now renders instantly, with the inventory streaming in behind a Suspense fallback. The cause: `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top level of the page component. Since that function calls `connection()`, it can only run at request time, and because it blocked the whole component, nothing — not even the static "Premium Widget" heading — could render until the server finished. The fix follows the pattern from this Next.js version's "Instant navigation" guide (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md`): I extracted the inventory fetch into a child `Inventory` component and wrapped it in `Checking availability...

}>`. The page component itself is now fully static, so the title is part of the prerendered shell and appears immediately on navigation, while the stock count and price stream into the fallback. Verified with `next build`: `/product` now builds as `◐ Partial Prerender` (static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content), and the prerendered shell in `.next/server/app/product.html` contains both "Premium Widget" and the "Checking availability..." fallback. Note the price is inside the Suspense boundary too since it comes from the same request-time `getInventory()` call — if the price should also be instant, it would need to be served from cached data instead (e.g. a `'use cache'` function).

Fixed — the product title now renders instantly, with the inventory streaming in behind a Suspense fallback. The cause: `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top level of the page component. Since that function calls `connection()`, it can only run at request time, and because it blocked the whole component, nothing — not even the static "Premium Widget" heading — could render until the server finished. The fix follows the pattern from this Next.js version's "Instant navigation" guide (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md`): I extracted the inventory fetch into a child `Inventory` component and wrapped it in `Checking availability...

}>`. The page component itself is now fully static, so the title is part of the prerendered shell and appears immediately on navigation, while the stock count and price stream into the fallback. Verified with `next build`: `/product` now builds as `◐ Partial Prerender` (static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content), and the prerendered shell in `.next/server/app/product.html` contains both "Premium Widget" and the "Checking availability..." fallback. Note the price is inside the Suspense boundary too since it comes from the same request-time `getInventory()` call — if the price should also be instant, it would need to be served from cached data instead (e.g. a `'use cache'` function).
